messages:
Maya Chen: Heads-up — canary in eu-west-1 shows a sharp p95 decode latency jump after last night's rollout. p95 +30% vs baseline. Noticed right after the mode-switch in kernel selector.
Raj Patel: Ugh. Which rollout? can you paste the canary id / PR?
Maya Chen: Canary id: canary-20260315-eu1. Linked PR was #4982 (kernel-selector: adaptive-mode-thresholds). Deployed ~02:18 UTC.
Lin Gómez: I saw CI perf alert earlier this morning: perf-ci/3987 flagged decode p95 regression on short-seq workload. Might be related.
Seb Turner: Any KV-cache anomalies? mode switches sometimes end up invalidating sticky kv segments and cause memcpys.
Maya Chen: KV ops look normal on metrics but cache hit ratio dropped ~4% during the spike window. attaching quick sample of the flamegraph + profile.
Maya Chen: ```
perf-binary-profile: https://internal.perf/reports/3276543210/flame.svg
summary:
 - decode_kernel_fast (quant_fused) 24% -> 12%
 - decode_kernel_generic (fallback) 10% -> 26%
 - kv_memcpy 2% -> 8%
``` 
Raj Patel: So kernel selector flipped workloads to generic kernel more often. Any recent changes in tiling/small-batch heuristics in #4982?
Lin Gómez: #4982 lowered the fast-path warmup threshold to 6 tokens (from 12) and changed a "sticky_segmentation" flag to true by default. That could cause smaller batches to choose generic path.
Seb Turner: If small-batch gets routed to generic decode kernel, p95 will suffer. The kv_memcpy increase suggests more KV churn (maybe eviction-driven).
Maya Chen: Repro instructions I used on canary box:
```bash
# reproduce sample load
./run_local_client --model redwood-serve-v2 --seq-len 16 --batch-distribution short:0.9,long:0.1 --concurrency 48 --region eu-west-1
# collect perf
perf record -g -o /tmp/perf.data -- ./runtime_server --config /etc/redwood/canary.conf
```
Raj Patel: Can someone try disabling sticky_segmentation on the canary to confirm? Patch idea: revert that flag and rerun canary for 30m.
Lin Gómez: I'm on it — toggling sticky_segmentation=false for canary and redeploying now. ETA ~12 minutes.
deploy-bot: deploy started: canary-20260315-eu1 -> config change sticky_segmentation=false (initiated by Lin Gómez).
perf-bot: ci:perf alert acknowledged perf-ci/3987 linked to thread 3276543210
Maya Chen: If this repros locally I'd also like a short bisect plan: suspect commits between 2026-03-14 22:00 and 02:00 UTC (around #4982 and #4969).
Seb Turner: Quick bisect idea: 1) revert sticky_segmentation switch only 2) if still bad, revert adaptive warmup threshold 3) if still bad, rollback #4969 (fused-op reorder). We should hold canary rollout until step 2 passes.
Raj Patel: I'll stand up a short bisect job that runs perf harness across those three toggles (fast path on/off, sticky on/off, fused-op reorder on/off). Linking job when ready.
Lin Gómez: Can confirm initial redeploy looks better — first 10m p95 down ~18% vs spike window. Will let it run full 30m and then post numbers.
Maya Chen: Great. If sticky_segmentation flip is the culprit we should add an integration test that validates kernel selection distribution under short-seq-heavy traffic.
Seb Turner: Agreed. Also add a guard in kernel-selector to bias away from generic kernel if batch size < X unless explicit fallback triggered.
Raj Patel: Bisect job up: https://ci.internal/bs/8242 — runs three permutations across canary workload. Will post results in ~45m.
Maya Chen: Thanks all. If bisect points to #4982 we'll plan a tiny revert and then run canary. Otherwise full rollback plan is on the table. :thumbsup:
perf-bot: perf-ci/3987 finished. tentative culprit: sticky_segmentation toggle in #4982. See CI diff: https://ci.internal/reports/3987/diff
Lin Gómez: Can confirm final numbers: after toggling sticky_segmentation=false p95 returned close to baseline (within 3%). Looks like winner.
Seb Turner: Ok let's revert the sticky default, keep the warmup threshold change, and add test + telemetry.
Maya Chen: I'll open the revert PR for just the sticky flag and add a short kernel-selection test. PR #4998 opened: revert sticky_segmentation default. Requesting review from @Seb Turner and @Raj Patel.
Raj Patel: Reviewing now. If green, promote to canary and then proceed with staged rollout.
Maya Chen: Closing loop: lesson — mode-switch heuristics can have non-obvious KV/cache interactions. We'll add a checklist for kernel-selector changes: perf harness + KV-hit smoke + short-seq bias test.
Seb Turner: Good postmortem fodder. :memo:
